::: {.resource-intro}
**The essential idea:** Ethical communication requires accurate attribution, honest representation of evidence, care for collaborators and communities, and transparency about tools used in producing work.
:::

## Core practices

### Attribute appropriately

Cite sources for ideas, data, images, and language; distinguish your analysis from others’ work.

### Respect people and materials

Protect personal, sensitive, confidential, and community-controlled information; follow consent and data-use restrictions.

### Use AI critically

Verify all claims and citations independently; do not share restricted content with tools; disclose use when required by the relevant setting.

## A simple workflow

For a draft, audit each factual claim and visual: locate its source, check whether it is represented fairly, document permissions or attribution, and write a brief record of any AI assistance and independent checks.

## In context

::: {.callout-example}
A student preparing a public map of ecological observations asks whether disclosing precise coordinates could expose sensitive species or culturally significant sites; they choose an appropriate geographic scale.
:::

## Keep in mind

Course, journal, institutional, funder, and community protocols may differ. Follow the requirements of the specific project and seek guidance when obligations conflict.
